title: Yeasty Russian Buckwheat Blini
description: A crispy and flavorful Russian dish featuring a nutmeg-infused yeast dough, perfect for a crowd-pleasing breakfast or snack.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the buckwheat flour, yeast, sugar, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the egg, milk, butter, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a smooth batter forms.
Let the batter rise in a warm place for about 1 hour.
Preheat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Using a ladle, pour the batter onto the skillet or griddle and cook for about 2 minutes on each side.
The blini should be crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside.
Serve the blini warm with your favorite toppings, such as sour cream, jam, or caviar.
To spherify the blini, dip them in a mixture of water and sodium alginate, and then drop them into a bath of water and calcium chloride.
Be careful not to overcook the blini, as they can become dry and crumbly.
To freeze the blini, place them on a baking sheet and put them in the freezer until they are frozen solid.
Then, transfer the frozen blini to a freezer-safe bag or container and store them in the freezer for up to 3 months.
When you are ready to cook the blini, simply thaw them overnight in the refrigerator or cook them straight from the freezer.
Cook the blini in a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat, cooking for about 2 minutes on each side.
Serve the blini hot with your favorite toppings, such as sour cream, jam, or caviar.
